subject.title: message tool: Feishu send action polluted by poll schema/guard prevents file send

question: Should the shared `message` tool continue exposing poll creation fields on ordinary `send`, or should OpenClaw split/scope/sanitize those fields so normal sends cannot be rejected by poll schema padding?
rationale: Current main intentionally permits metadata-only padding but still rejects content-bearing poll fields on `send`; choosing between stricter poll intent, param stripping, or action-specific schemas changes the model-facing tool contract.

options.title: Action-scope or split poll schema
options.body: Expose poll creation fields only for the poll action or channel-specific poll tools, reducing accidental model fill while preserving strict poll validation.

options.title: Strip poll params on send
options.body: Sanitize all poll creation fields from `action="send"` before the guard, preserving the unified schema but making send tolerant of overfilled params.

options.title: Keep current guard
options.body: Accept that content-bearing poll fields reject `send`, and require live evidence before changing the tool contract further.

recommendation.title: Action-scope or split poll schema
recommendation.body: Expose poll creation fields only for the poll action or channel-specific poll tools, reducing accidental model fill while preserving strict poll validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent outbound/tool contract history makes this the strongest available owner for the product-shape decision.
